title: [v0.5.0] Release: freeze the complete BaseHarbor contract
author: mcpdev80
body:
## Goal

Freeze and stabilize the runtime-neutral BaseHarbor language and semantics completed in v0.4.

v0.5 deliberately adds no new platform primitive, runtime or major capability.

> **Developer experience first.**
>
> **Simple by default. Secure by default. Explicit when needed.**
>
> **As little as possible, as much as necessary.**

## Freeze target

v0.4 establishes:

```text
Portable Intent
   ↓
Environment + Policy
   ↓
Capability / Provider Resolution
   ↓
Placement / Ownership
   ↓
Plan / Preflight
   ↓
Provision / Bind
   ↓
Observe / Reconcile
   ↓
Verify
   ↓
Audit / Evidence
```

v0.5 makes the compatibility guarantees around this model explicit and dependable.

Compose remains the complete reference runtime. Kubernetes is a later runtime track and must consume the frozen semantics rather than force a redesign.

## Scope

- contract/schema versioning;
- capability-spec versioning;
- capability-provider protocol compatibility;
- machine result/error schema versioning;
- persisted state compatibility/migration rules;
- deprecation rules;
- upgrade compatibility from supported v0.4 state;
- full security/ownership review;
- documentation reconciliation;
- exact-head conformance/acceptance;
- packaging/release hardening;
- release artifacts and metadata consistency.

## Developer experience

The normal path remains:

```bash
git clone <app>
cd <app>
baha app init
baha up
```

The freeze must not introduce migration ceremony for normal users without a demonstrated need.

Requirements:

- final pre-freeze defaults remain simple;
- v0.5.0 establishes the first frozen compatibility baseline;
- no migration/deprecation ceremony is required for obsolete pre-freeze-only behavior;
- CLI/JSON/MCP remain consistent adapters over one core;
- no runtime/provider implementation detail is added to portable intent.

## Agent-native Compose completeness

The complete agent-native lifecycle is implemented before the freeze in v0.4.15 / #403. Before the contract freeze is considered complete, BaseHarbor must revalidate that a generic coding agent can operate the supported BaseHarbor lifecycle without falling back to raw shell/Docker/Compose/Podman execution.

This does **not** mean mirroring every CLI command 1:1 into MCP.

The frozen machine/agent surface must preserve the complete useful BaseHarbor lifecycle established by #403 through a small semantic API over the same shared core.

Required lifecycle coverage, where the corresponding capability exists:

```text
discover
  ↓
inspect
  ↓
plan
  ↓
apply / up
  ↓
status
  ↓
doctor
  ↓
observe diagnostics
  ↓
update
  ↓
backup
  ↓
restore
  ↓
drift / repair
  ↓
destroy
```

Rules:

- CLI, JSON and MCP use the same domain/lifecycle logic;
- MCP must not expose generic shell, Docker or Compose execution;
- read-only, mutating and destructive operations retain explicit safety metadata;
- destructive operations preserve confirmation/approval semantics;
- policy, ownership, preflight, reconciliation, verification and evidence cannot be bypassed;
- machine output remains secret-safe;
- observability data should use the smallest useful semantic resource/tool surface instead of duplicating every CLI presentation command;
- unsupported lifecycle operations must fail explicitly rather than force an agent to escape to raw runtime tooling.

The goal is:

> A capable generic coding agent can operate BaseHarbor end-to-end on Compose using BaseHarbor semantics only.

## Compatibility question

v0.5 is ready only when the answer is yes:

> Can a later runtime provider, including Kubernetes, implement the frozen BaseHarbor semantics without requiring a fundamental rewrite of the portable application contract?

This does not require Kubernetes implementation in v0.5.

## v0.4 completion dependency

The contract freeze begins only after:

```text
v0.4.17 / #363  Managed application identity/authentication
        ↓
v0.4.18 / #210  Capability Provider SDK + conformance
        ↓
v0.4.19 / #516  Messaging + Key-Value DB + Document DB contracts/reference providers
        ↓
v0.4.20 / #519  Source-neutral repository adoption / Workload Source Adapters
        ↓
v0.4.21 / #174  Full-stack semantic + pre-freeze architecture acceptance
        ↓
v0.5.0  Contract freeze
```

Managed application identity (#363) is therefore part of the pre-freeze contract. BaseHarbor operator/human OIDC/RBAC/JIT remains deferred in #100.

## v0.5 release sequence

- **v0.5.0 / #175 — Contract freeze and revalidation of the completed agent-native core**
  - public contract inventory and versioning;
  - state-boundary and runtime/provider-boundary freeze;
  - additive vs breaking change rules;
  - no new platform primitive.

- **v0.5.1 / #297 — State versioning and migration compatibility**
  - deterministic state versions and migrations;
  - non-mutating migration preflight;
  - verification and fail-closed recovery behavior.

- **v0.5.2 / #298 — Cross-component compatibility contracts**
  - CLI/Core/application/state/provider/machine compatibility boundaries;
  - capability-provider and runtime-provider separation;
  - Kubernetes/OpenShift/AWS/Azure/GCP neutrality gates.

- **v0.5.3 / #299 — Upgrade, recovery and deprecation behavior**
  - safe upgrade flow;
  - recovery/rollback where appropriate;
  - bounded, actionable deprecation behavior.

- **v0.5.4 / #300 — Portability and compatibility acceptance**
  - exact-head acceptance;
  - Compose reference lifecycle;
  - migration/provider/machine-contract compatibility;
  - portability review for Kubernetes/OpenShift/AWS/Azure/GCP.

## Explicitly deferred

- availability/HA/topology semantics;
- Kubernetes runtime implementation;
- Operator/CRDs;
- OpenShift/enterprise runtime;
- BaseHarbor operator/human OIDC, RBAC, JIT and breakglass access (#100);
- private-registry/air-gap implementation;
- optional ecosystem breadth.

## Release gates

- [ ] v0.5.0 explicitly establishes the first frozen compatibility baseline without requiring migration from obsolete pre-freeze-only state.
- [ ] Portable/deployment/runtime/provider state boundaries are documented.
- [ ] Structured machine-output schemas are versioned.
- [ ] Capability-provider contract/conformance is documented.
- [ ] Security and ownership review passes.
- [ ] Human CLI, JSON and MCP demonstrably use shared domain/lifecycle logic.
- [ ] A generic coding agent can complete the supported Compose lifecycle end to end through BaseHarbor MCP/JSON without raw shell/Docker/Compose fallback.
- [ ] Machine/agent coverage includes discover, inspect, plan, apply/up, status, doctor, update, backup, restore, drift/repair and destroy wherever those lifecycle operations are supported by BaseHarbor.
- [ ] MCP remains a small semantic surface and does not become a 1:1 CLI wrapper or generic runtime-execution interface.
- [ ] Five-minute onboarding is validated from a clean environment.
- [ ] Canonical documentation matches actual behavior.
- [ ] Exact final implementation head is validated economically.
- [ ] Local/repository validation is used first where practical; GitHub Actions only where required.
- [ ] Human-friendly release notes exist.
- [ ] Changelog, tag, source and release metadata agree.
- [ ] Release artifacts are verified.


## Pre-freeze architecture gate

v0.5.0 must not freeze the public contract until the v0.4 acceptance review (#174) has explicitly closed the following boundaries:

- [ ] managed application identity/authentication boundary (#363);
- [ ] secrets and credential ownership boundary;
- [ ] network/connectivity and exposure boundary;
- [ ] storage/state ownership boundary;
- [ ] artifact/distribution and supply-chain identity boundary;
- [ ] PKI/certificate/trust lifecycle boundary;
- [ ] backup/restore/recovery semantics;
- [ ] audit/evidence semantics;
- [ ] ownership and placement semantics;
- [ ] runtime/capability/delivery separation;
- [ ] workload-source / repository-adoption boundary (#519);
- [ ] CLI/JSON/MCP semantic parity.

The gate is about **contract sufficiency**, not ecosystem breadth.

It does not require shipping pgAdmin, Keycloak Admin UI, Valkey Admin, Grafana, AI, vector search, Kubernetes, cloud providers, air-gap support or other optional integrations beyond the explicitly scheduled pre-freeze capabilities in #516.

If review discovers a genuinely missing portable primitive, fix that primitive before the freeze. If the gap is only product-specific tooling or convenience, defer it.

## Core freeze rule

Post-v0.5 core changes require a genuine missing platform primitive. Product-, runtime-, IDE- or vendor-specific shortcuts do not justify contaminating portable semantics.

Parent roadmap: #155
v0.4 semantic acceptance: #174
Deferred ecosystem: #209


## Kubernetes readiness of the frozen contract

v0.5 must freeze enough runtime-neutral deployment semantics that Kubernetes can be added later without changing the portable application contract.

This does **not** mean adding Kubernetes fields early.

The freeze must distinguish three layers explicitly:

```text
1. Portable application intent
   what the application needs

2. Deployment / operator state
   where and under which platform conditions it runs

3. Runtime/provider realization
   how the selected runtime/provider implements it
```

### Target contract freeze

The Target/Access/Scope model is established before v0.5 by **#408 / v0.4.15**.

v0.5 does not invent or reshape that model. It freezes and revalidates it together with the rest of the BaseHarbor core contract.

The frozen identity is:

```text
Deployment = Target + Application + Environment
```

and Target continues to reference:

```text
Runtime Provider
Access Reference
Scope
```

Freeze acceptance:

- Target state remains deployment/operator state, not portable application intent;
- Target-scoped runtime/deployment state from #408 is part of the persisted compatibility surface;
- changing Target never rewrites portable application intent;
- Runtime Providers consume the resolved Target contract rather than redefining it;
- CLI, JSON and MCP preserve the same effective deployment identity.

### Runtime access compatibility

Access definitions are already part of the #408 Target contract.

v0.5 freezes their secret-safe reference semantics; it does not define a new access model.

Acceptance:

- Access remains referenced outside portable application intent;
- credential material itself is never migrated into portable application state;
- provider-native authentication details remain behind Runtime Provider interpretation;
- compatibility/versioning applies to persisted Access metadata where BaseHarbor owns it.


### Platform resource references

Later runtimes must be able to consume platform-owned resources without BaseHarbor owning or creating them.

The deployment/operator boundary must support references to platform resources such as future:

- shared ingress/gateway infrastructure;
- storage policy/class;
- namespace/project;
- platform identity/trust integration;
- platform policy/profile.

These references must remain opaque/runtime-owned where possible.

Do not add Kubernetes names such as `GatewayClass`, `StorageClass` or `namespace` to portable application intent.

### Permission/capability-aware outcomes

The frozen semantic result model must be able to distinguish at least:

- supported;
- unsupported;
- unverifiable;
- denied/not authorized;
- conflict;
- foreign-owned;
- degraded;
- failed verification.

This is required so a later restricted runtime can fail only the feature that lacks permissions/capability instead of collapsing the entire application lifecycle.



## Existing target scope semantics

A deployment target may point at an already existing runtime scope with an arbitrary platform-assigned name.

Example future Kubernetes realization:

```text
runtime: kubernetes
target scope: r2-4b-dt-test
scope ownership: platform/external
```

The application contract does not need to know or own that name.

Rules:

- the runtime provider interprets the generic deployment target scope using runtime-specific semantics;
- Kubernetes interprets the target scope as the existing namespace;
- BaseHarbor must not rename or recreate a platform-owned target scope merely to match application/environment naming;
- multiple BaseHarbor applications may coexist in one existing namespace when platform policy allows it;
- BaseHarbor ownership must therefore be tracked below namespace level using stable BaseHarbor application/environment/resource identity;
- `baha destroy` removes only BaseHarbor-owned application resources from a platform/external target scope;
- `baha destroy` must never delete a platform/external namespace itself;
- namespace deletion is permitted only when the namespace is explicitly BaseHarbor-owned and the selected lifecycle/policy allows it.



## Capability semantic compatibility freeze

The v0.5 freeze includes the rule that capability compatibility is semantic, not nominal.

A plan must not consider a provider compatible merely because it advertises the same capability identifier.

The frozen contract must support a versioned way to express and negotiate application-relevant capability semantics when the default capability contract is insufficient.

Hard boundaries:

- normal intent stays sparse;
- absence means the capability's defined default/common semantic contract;
- only demonstrated non-default application requirements become explicit;
- provider-specific implementation details do not become portable intent;
- semantic feature compatibility is separate from v0.6 availability/topology guarantees;
- a missing required semantic is unsupported, not degraded success.



## Delivery-provider freeze boundary

The v0.5 contract freeze must preserve delivery as an independent deployment concern:

```text
runtime != capability != delivery
```

The frozen model must support:

- direct delivery, where BaseHarbor performs runtime mutation/reconciliation;
- delegated delivery, where a Delivery Provider publishes/requests desired realization and an external reconciler performs runtime mutation;
- explicit reconciliation ownership;
- typed delivery/synchronization states;
- application/shared/external provider placement where applicable;
- provider-neutral desired revision/reference identity.

No Argo CD, Flux, Git-provider, Helm or Kubernetes-specific fields enter portable application intent.

The purpose is architectural readiness only. A real GitOps reference provider is implemented later in #325.


## Pre-release gate

Before creating this release:

- [ ] All acceptance criteria in this issue are complete.
- [ ] Required local/repository tests pass.
- [ ] The full relevant CI matrix has passed at least once on the **exact release-candidate commit**.
- [ ] Docker and Podman acceptance pass where applicable.
- [ ] Security, isolation and secret-leak checks pass where applicable.
- [ ] The documentation audit defined by #364 passes.
- [ ] Human-facing documentation matches the shipped behavior.
- [ ] Reference and normative specs match every changed public contract.
- [ ] No unresolved release blocker remains.
- [ ] Version, changelog, release notes and release metadata are consistent.
- [ ] Final exact-head acceptance evidence is recorded before tagging/releasing.

Acceptance answers whether the feature/release scope is complete. This gate answers whether the exact commit is safe and documented well enough to release.

Do not weaken or skip a required check merely to complete the release. Checks that are genuinely not applicable should be recorded as such rather than silently omitted.


## Provider Catalog and descriptor freeze boundary

v0.5.0 freezes the discovery/distribution contract needed for an open provider ecosystem without turning the catalog into runtime state.

BaseHarbor distinguishes:

```text
Provider Catalog
  -> what provider implementations exist and can be resolved

Provider Runtime Registry
  -> what provider instances are installed/running/bound here
```

The existing runtime/provider instance registry remains authoritative for instance, binding, placement and ownership state. It is not replaced by the Provider Catalog.

The Provider Catalog uses one common catalog model with three provider families:

```text
RuntimeProvider
CapabilityProvider
DeliveryProvider
```

Hard rule:

```text
runtime != capability != delivery
```

The frozen catalog/descriptor model must define at least:

- provider family/kind;
- stable provider ID;
- provider implementation version;
- Provider Protocol version compatibility;
- supported service/capability contract versions where applicable;
- protocol/capability declarations where applicable;
- supported platforms;
- OCI artifact reference;
- authoritative content digest;
- schema/descriptor version;
- provenance/signature metadata references where supported.

Distribution must reuse OCI standards rather than introduce a proprietary BaseHarbor blob/package format.

The descriptor/catalog contract is discovery metadata. Provider execution still uses the Provider Integration Contract, and instantiated/bound provider state remains deployment/runtime state.

Standards-first rules:

- OCI Distribution/Image/Artifact conventions are the distribution baseline;
- digest identity is authoritative; tags are human-friendly references;
- JSON Schema 2020-12 is the canonical schema format for catalog/service descriptors where JSON Schema applies;
- existing open standards are preferred over Baha-specific fields;
- Baha extensions must be versioned and limited to semantics not covered by adopted standards.

v0.5.0 does not require a public marketplace, hosted registry service, search UI or ecosystem breadth. It freezes the contract needed to add those later without redesigning Core.

### Provider Catalog freeze acceptance

- [ ] Provider Catalog and Provider Runtime Registry are documented as separate boundaries.
- [ ] One catalog contract can describe Runtime, Capability and Delivery Provider families without merging their responsibilities.
- [ ] Provider descriptors are versioned and machine-validatable.
- [ ] OCI artifact reference + digest are part of the frozen provider distribution identity.
- [ ] Catalog metadata does not become portable application intent.
- [ ] Existing provider instance/binding/ownership state remains authoritative runtime state and is not duplicated into the catalog.
- [ ] No proprietary BaseHarbor artifact transport/package format is required for provider distribution.


## Runtime-provider freeze prerequisite

The v0.5.0 contract freeze MUST NOT freeze the current Compose-coupled transitional runtime seam.

Before this issue closes:

- #396 must be complete;
- the standards-first runtime-provider semantic boundary must be stable enough to version as v1;
- Docker and Podman must prove the boundary as reference implementations;
- concrete runtime products must not be required knowledge in portable Core semantics;
- adopted standards versus BaseHarbor extensions must be explicitly documented.

The freeze covers the semantic compatibility boundary, not any one runtime product implementation.


## MCP completion prerequisite

The agent-native implementation itself is no longer deferred to v0.5.

It is completed in:

```text
v0.4.15
#397 secure service access
  ↓
#398 complete observability semantics
  ↓
#403 complete agent-native MCP/JSON lifecycle
```

Every later v0.4 release (#399, #212, #210, #363, #174) carries an explicit MCP/machine-interface parity gate. Therefore v0.5.0 freezes and validates an already complete, continuously maintained agent-native contract rather than catching up missing MCP functionality at freeze time.

Freeze acceptance MUST prove that the final v0.4.21 semantics are represented consistently across CLI, JSON and MCP.


## Pre-freeze compatibility rule

v0.5.0 freezes the final converged contract; it does NOT promise migration compatibility from obsolete pre-freeze v0.4 development-state formats or command shapes.

Hard rule:

```text
pre-freeze v0.4
    -> converge freely on the correct model

v0.5.0
    -> establish the compatibility baseline

post-freeze v0.5.x+
    -> version/migrate/deprecate from frozen contracts
```

Do not carry legacy modes, aliases, state migration layers or compatibility shims into v0.5.0 solely because an earlier v0.4 development release used a different shape.


## Developer access and credential portability freeze prerequisite

- #777 — developer access, credential portability and profile export/import

The v0.5.0 freeze must not begin until #777 is complete. The frozen baseline must preserve frictionless local development without mandatory BaseHarbor login, standards-first Git/SSH/kubeconfig/cloud authentication, explicit temporary-vs-secure credential persistence, recoverable secure local credentials, and a strict separation between developer profile export/import, application recovery and remote platform disaster recovery.


---

## Pre-freeze scheduling clarification (2026-10-10)
#904/v0.4.30 delivers TLS/proxy and attack-protection work (#902/#903). Complete #872–#876, #904 and the final semantic acceptance #174 (v0.4.31), then a no-new-features stability/reconciliation cycle before formal #175/v0.5 freeze. Contract intent specified in #872, implemented and qualified incrementally; no freeze without actual evidence.

comments.body:
## Freeze criterion: standards-first contract boundary

#391 is now an explicit prerequisite for the v0.5 freeze.

Before this issue closes:
- JSON Schema 2020-12 is the canonical portable service/provider schema dialect.
- Service Binding 1.1 well-known connection names are authoritative where applicable.
- service vs protocol vs provider vs product/version axes are frozen separately.
- provider catalog metadata is distinct from runtime provider-instance registry state.
- current v0.4 capability IDs have explicit compatibility/migration classification.
- OTel/OIDC/AsyncAPI/CloudEvents/RESP/S3 compatibility semantics are correctly located and no product contract leaks into portable intent.
